decisions.reason: Its weaker post-launch visibility, delayed/limited release, and narrower particle-therapy niche suggest enough uncertainty has resolved to show lower payoff than other core dosimetry options, so resources are better redeployed.

As a small-volume ionization chamber tightly aligned with the firm's core dosimetry and calibration capabilities, it remains a relatively low-cost option to keep open in a specialist market where adoption can take time.

This chamber sits squarely in the firm's established measurement portfolio and likely benefits from shared certification, service, and customer relationships, making continued market presence worthwhile while demand matures.
A standard clinical ionization chamber is close to the firm's core business and likely has steady strategic value with modest incremental carrying cost, so there is little reason to abandon it early.
Relative-dosimetry chambers complement the firm's broader QA workflow offering and preserve cross-selling and installed-base value, which supports keeping the option active.

A thimble ionization chamber is a familiar, core-category product for this type of radiation-physics supplier, and maintaining it likely costs less than the option value of serving ongoing clinical needs.
